text: Machine Girl (sometimes stylized as machin3gir1) is an American electronic music project founded in 2012 by Matt Stephenson, also known as DJ Chaotic Ugly, on Long Island, New York. In 2015, the project expanded into a duo when Stephenson recruited percussionist Sean Kelly to play live drums. Lucy Caputi joined in 2024 as a live guitarist and official member. In 2022, Machine Girl composed the original soundtrack for the video game Neon White, consisting of two parts—"The Wicked Heart" and "The Burn That Cures"—aligned with the game's narrative. In an interview with Revolver magazine, Stephenson described the project as "fucked-up electronic punk" and rejected the "industrial" label for being "very goth, and very black and white," emphasizing its "a lot more colorful" nature. Kerrang! recognized Machine Girl as one of the "bands expanding the definition of hardcore," characterizing them as "a particularly punky and ferocious breed of the electronic sub-genre breakcore that could easily pass for hardcore when they rip it live." Pitchfork defined their sound as "relentlessly smashing together bits of punk, grindcore, rave, industrial, and more," describing it as "unpredictable and dangerous, full of animalistic rage and uncontrollable energy." The project's name originates from the 2008 Japanese film The Machine Girl, which they occasionally sampled on their 2014 album WLFGRL. Stephenson is also a member of the electronic duo Prolaps with Bonnie Baxter from Kill Alters, beginning their collaboration on the track "Vomit" from ...Because I'm Young Arrogant and Hate Everything You Stand For, which they started releasing in 2020. In 2013, Machine Girl began posting self-directed videos on their YouTube channel, starting with the unfinished song "~*•°•.[g0o∂]_[∫3º¥].•°•*~," released on December 20, 2013. Their next upload was on February 7, 2014, for the song "Ginger Claps," nine days before the release of their debut album WLFGRL. On November 4, 2014, they posted a video titled "___________DJPH11252014," promoting a DJ performance at "DJ PHANTASY CLUB" featuring ABSRDST, Doss, DV-i, Ducky, Machine Girl, Ligaments, Legion, and The Magick Report, including a snippet of an early mix of "Loop Version" that later appeared on their 2018 album The Ugly Art. On July 31, 2015, Machine Girl released two videos titled "HEAVEN MIX" and "HELL MIX," featuring visuals by Videopunks and containing snippets from each side of their sophomore album Gemini. The next official music video was for "Bitten Twice," released on May 16, 2017, followed by "Sad Claps" on June 12, 2017. Subsequent visualizers were uploaded for ...Because I'm Young Arrogant and Hate Everything You Stand For (September 24, 2017), MRK90 MIX VOL 1 (December 17, 2017), and The Ugly Art (October 14, 2018). The next music video to be published was for "Fully In It" on August 28, 2020, featuring stop motion animation by Ellie Thatcher. On November 15, 2020, Machine Girl released a video titled "GLOBAL FANDEMIC [MACHINE GIRL SET @ A2B2 NIGHT OF FIRE]" as part of a 24-hour virtual music festival hosted by Andy Morin of a2b2, featuring Matt performing over fan-submitted visualizers and including almost entirely unreleased songs and a shortened version of "Athoth A Go!! Go!!" with a different bassline, as well as an early demo of "Just Because You Can," which later appeared on their 2024 album MG Ultra. A visualizer for Prolaps' album Guilted Hexitation was posted on January 3, 2021, titled "PROLAPS 2021 GUILTED HEXITATION," shot by Nicos Kennedy and edited by Lana Evoli. A visualizer for Ultra Cycle Pt. 1: Vernal Birth premiered on March 21, 2021, with visuals by Lucid Interval, followed by a video for Ultra Cycle Pt. 2: Estival Growth on June 22, 2021, featuring visuals by N3T4. On August 28, 2024, Machine Girl released an official music video for "Until I Die," from the album MG Ultra, directed by Bryan M. Ferguson. A week later, on September 4, 2024, they released a music video for "Motherfather" from the same album. Despite resembling AI-generated art, the video was confirmed to contain no AI-generated assets, as stated by director John Lee. On October 4, 2024, they released a music video for "Psychic Attack," the final track of MG Ultra. Two months later, on December 13, 2024, they released a music video for "Ass2Mars," another MG Ultra song, directed by Sandy Loaf. A video for "Grindhouse," another track from MG Ultra, premiered on January 1, 2025, directed, filmed, and edited by Sydney Villacortabuer, and features scenes of a fight at a supernatural party.
